Alyssa / team — attaching the sizing workbook (gpu_pool_sizing_estimate.xlsx). High level notes: 

1) Baseline eval tranche (MVP): 4x H100-equivalent nodes (32GB VRAM) when running quantized models — supports 10 concurrent long-context sessions and batched reranking jobs. Estimated steady token throughput for your test prompts: ~1.2M tokens/day.

2) Heavy-context eval: 6x H100 nodes or 8x when you include parallel offline retraining/embedding jobs.

3) Lead-time assumptions (conservative): 
   - Hosted Dedicated: order+contract sign → provisioning (staging) = 28–42 days.
   - Private (VPC) with KMS: 45–70 days (network handshakes + compliance checks).
   - On-prem (customer-supplied): estimate 60–120 days (depends on rack/cabling/acceptance).

4) Phasing recommendation (to reduce up-front spend): 
   - Phase 0 (Eval week 0–3): 4x nodes in a shared reserved pool with aggressive KV cache enabled + sample traffic replay.
   - Phase 1 (Post-eval weeks 4–8): expand to 6x nodes, enable continuous batching and A/B fallback to lower-precision model if tail latency spikes.
   - Phase 2 (Production on-ramp 9–12): ramp to target pool (8–12 nodes) with canary routing and per-route SLOs.

5) Acceptance gates we suggest adding to the MAP (we can write the language):
   - Functional: end-to-end flows pass smoke tests (latency and correctness) on staging.
   - Performance: 95th percentile latency ≤ 150ms for gen flows under production-like concurrency.
   - Ops: monitoring/tracing hooks and token-level cost reports available to Novamed.

If you want, I can convert the phasing notes into a 1-page procurement brief that procurement can use for budget sign-off.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
